title: Things to Do in Denver When You're Dead

sections.content: Following the path of neo-noir crime dramas, 'Things to Do in Denver When You're Dead' centers on Jimmy 'The Saint' Tosnia (Andy Garcia), a former gangster trying to go straight with a legitimate business venture. When his former boss, the paralyzed crime lord The Man With The Plan (Christopher Walken), forces him to do one last job, Jimmy assembles a crew of distinctive characters for what should be a simple intimidation scheme. When the plan goes horrifically wrong, Jimmy and his crew are given 'buckwheats' - a death sentence that promises a slow, painful end - and must spend their final days making peace with their impending doom.

sections.content: The film shines through its exceptional ensemble cast. Garcia brings a smooth dignity to Jimmy, while Walken delivers one of his most menacing performances as the wheelchair-bound kingpin. Director Gary Fleder orchestrates the proceedings with stylish flair, creating a modern noir atmosphere that pays homage to classics like **The Killing** (1956) while establishing its own unique voice. The film's criminal argot - including terms like 'boat drinks' and 'give it a name' - creates a distinctive underworld vocabulary that enhances the film's unique identity.

sections.content: Released in the wake of **Pulp Fiction** (1994), the film represents the 1990s trend of dialogue-driven crime films that mixed violence with philosophical contemplation. It explores themes of redemption, loyalty, and the possibility of escaping one's past, while adding its own meditation on how people face death with dignity. The film's exploration of honor among thieves recalls **Miller's Crossing** (1990), while its fatalistic tone echoes **The Killing** (1956).

sections.content: The film stands as a notable entry in the post-Tarantino crime film renaissance, alongside works like **Reservoir Dogs** (1992) and **The Usual Suspects** (1995). It distinguishes itself through its more melancholic tone and focus on mortality, sharing thematic DNA with earlier noir classics like **Touch of Evil** (1958) while incorporating modern sensibilities.

sections.content: The film's meditation on mortality and redemption remains powerful, while its exploration of loyalty in an honor-less world resonates with contemporary crime dramas like **Drive** (2011) and **Hell or High Water** (2016). Its blend of stylish criminality with existential themes continues to influence modern neo-noir filmmaking.
